reading_note: The teaching distinguishes two registers within the spiritual organism: the interior, living members of the regenerate form (whose violation produces immediate spiritual pain because they are conjoined with life itself) and the exterior outgrowths — hair, nails, pruned shoots — which correspond to peripheral, ultimate truths and habitual outflows that may be cut away without injury and that regenerate of themselves. The arc moves from observation (pain when limbs are severed, none when extremities are trimmed) through the governing correspondence (the body is the natural ground, its members are trees rooted in that ground), to the discrimination of three classes of spiritual growth: trees that, transplanted, take root and grow again; trees that, when cut, do not regrow; and outgrowths perpetually renewed from the impurities of the food — i.e. falsities and concupiscences continually produced from the natural's appropriation of unclean nourishment, expressed in flesh that arouses desire. The teaching thus teaches discernment between the inviolable interior life and the prunable, regrowable, or wholly-to-be-cut exteriors.
